description: The countries of the UBL example world, with their currencies, tax schemes and identifier and address schemes. XU, XB and XL are ISO 3166-1 user-assigned codes; tools/build_codelists.py adds them and the world currencies to copies of the UBL 2.5 default code lists. Tax scheme identifiers are UN/EDIFACT 5153 codes (VAT, STT state/provincial sales tax, CUD customs duty, IMP import tax).

XU.name: Urvania
XU.note: Mainland, in the west: a rugged coast without a deep-water port, and the river down to Lumeport. Raw materials, manufacturing and power.

currency.name: Ferra
currency.note: ISO 4217 style: the country code and the initial of the currency's name; checked against the current ISO 4217 list. No minor unit: amounts are whole ferra, as with the Japanese yen.

wiki.lead: The **ferra** is the currency of [[Urvania]]. It has no minor unit: amounts are counted in whole ferra.

sections.title: Exchange
sections.text: Since 1996 the ferra has stood at a fixed parity with its partners' currencies under the [[Lumeport Trade Accord]]: a hundred ferra make one lume, and two hundred and fifty make one coral. Until then Urvania's protected economy kept the ferra apart.

tax.summary: Value added tax: charged at every stage, deducted by businesses, not charged on exports.

schemes.name: Value added tax
schemes.exports: not charged; the export is shown with its exemption reason

schemes.name: Energy tax
schemes.levied_on: electricity, per kWh delivered in the month
schemes.note: An excise in ferra per kWh, lower above 50,000 kWh a month for industry; value added tax is charged on the price plus the energy tax. The tiers apply to a customer's month as a whole; where the bill covers several connections, the supplier's statement per connection counts the lower tier on the main connection, so that the statements add up to the bill.

tax.exemption_codes_note: The exemption reasons as codes of Urvania's national list (XU:TaxExemptionReason).

inward_processing.holder: A company established in Urvania holds the authorisation; customs names in it the offices that may accept its entries and the period within which the goods must be discharged.
inward_processing.entry: Goods of a foreign owner are entered for inward processing: no duty and no import VAT is charged while they are worked.
inward_processing.release: When the processed products are released for free circulation, the duty and the import VAT are assessed, at the declarant's request, on the goods as they were placed under the procedure: their tariff line, customs value, quantity and origin on the day the entry was accepted.
inward_processing.supplies: Goods may be sold while they remain under the procedure; such a sale carries no Urvanian VAT, which is charged once, as import VAT on the importer, when the goods are released.
inward_processing.statistics: Trade statistics record the goods when they enter the procedure, at the value they would be invoiced at; their later release into free circulation is not recorded again.
inward_processing._refs: O150, O251 (checked against the EU texts, coordinator's source check 2026-11-20: duty and VAT on the goods placed on request, statistics on entry)

tax_id.format: XU and 9 digits, the last a check digit (weights 9..2, modulus 11)

address.line_rule: A line is made of the fields named in it, in that order, separated by a space; a field the address does not have is left out, and a line without any field is left out. A field with two language versions (street and town names in a bilingual country) gives both on the line, the national language first, then ' / ', then English: the building number is written once. Fields that are not on a line (ID, AddressTypeCode, CountrySubentityCode, TimezoneOffset, LocationCoordinate) say something other than where the post goes. The country is the last line of a postal address and is not repeated in the lines.
address.postal_codes_note: The post office's codes: the capital by its quarters (4100 to 4180), every other place one code of its own (O152 stage 2 B).

public_registry.name: Index of Public Administrations of Urvania
public_registry.keeper: the Agency for Digital Administration of Urvania
public_registry.id_format: xu_ and four lower-case letters or digits
public_registry.note: Every body of Urvania's public administration (the customs administration, the chambers of commerce, Codana and the other agencies set up by law) is entered in the index on its accreditation and given a code of its own, on the model of Italy's IPA code: the index assigns the code, and it is derived from no other register, not from the body's tax number.

statutory_interest.note: Urvania's statutory interest on late payment between businesses, which applies wherever the parties agreed nothing on late payment.

XU.history: An Italian territory, then under British rule, independent since 1962 as a bilingual country: Urvanian and English are its official languages. wiki.short: Country on the west of the mainland, member of the Lumeport Trade Accord
wiki.lead: **Urvania** is the western of the two countries of the mainland, with about {population} people. It holds the volcanic massif of the north-west, the green western hills and all the land south of the Runmek. Its capital is [[Ferrano]], the old Urvanian town of Ruldraz below the rapids. Urvania is bilingual: Urvanian and English are its official languages. Its currency is the {currency} ({currency_code}).

sections.title: Geography
sections.text:
Urvania covers about 90,500 km². A volcanic massif in the north-west, the Mukrir (Italian *Massiccio del Padre*, father), rises to about 1,920 m at the Cima Bianca; the [[Runmek]] rises on it at about 1,510 m and runs through a rift valley to the sea. Just above [[Ferrano]] it falls through rapids, which end navigation; below them the river carries barges to the estuary. The western hills and the land south of the river are green and hilly, wet from the westerly winds. From the border crossing the Runmek forms the border with [[Bayvarra]] down to the sea; north of the crossing the border follows the watershed, so that Urvania keeps the whole valley of the largest plateau river, the [[Bruna (river)|Bruna]].

Urvania lies in the belt of the South Atlantic high, about 30° south. Its summers, from November to March, are dry and sunny, with light north-east winds and about 23 °C on the coast; its winters, from May to September, bring the westerly winds, the fronts and the clouds, at about 17 °C on the coast. The rainiest months are March to June, the autumn and the start of winter. The westerlies drop their rain on the massif and the western hills, so the west and the high ground are wet and the south-east, around Saline Brune, is the driest and sunniest land. The massif's summit, about 12 °C colder than the coast, has snow in some winters.

The Urvanians call their heartland, the rift valley of the [[Runmek]], the Gamir (the valley). The wet hills of the west are the Colli Piovosi (Urvanian *Skarbek*, rain), the sunny hills of the south-east the Colli del Sole (*Vidrek*, sun), and the rugged south coast, without a deep-water port, the Costa Ligure, after the Ligurian fishermen who settled at Marina Ligure.

sections.title: Government
sections.text: Urvania is a parliamentary republic under its constitution of 1962. The president, its head of state, is elected by parliament for seven years. Parliament has a Chamber of Deputies and a Senate elected by the provinces, and the government, a prime minister with a council of ministers, answers to it.

sections.title: History
sections.text:
Before the Europeans came, the Urvanians farmed the wet valley of the Runmek and the hills west of it; their town, Ruldraz, grew where the valleys meet, below the rapids. In 1609–10 a voyage from Tuscany reached Ruldraz and founded a small trading post, which lasted some decades and faded in the 18th century; it left Ferrano's quarter Borgo Toscano and the chapel of San Ranieri del Guado.

In 1840 the Sardinian corvette *Euridice* sailed up the river to Ruldraz. The Urvanian rulers signed a treaty of protection with Sardinia at Ruldraz on 4 September 1840, and in 1842 Forte Euridice was built at the confluence of the Runmek and the [[Bruna (river)|Bruna]]. A boundary convention of 1857 set the border with the British colony to the east. In 1861 the Kingdom of Italy inherited the protectorate, and Urvania stayed an Italian territory until 1941, when British forces took it and put it under British administration; Italy renounced it in the peace treaty of 1947. On 17 June 1951, after years of asking, the Urvanians won official status for their language beside English, in the courts, the schools and the administration; the day is kept as Language Day.

Urvania became independent on 9 March 1962, by an agreement with Britain that ended its administration, bilingual in Urvanian and English. A constituent assembly elected that spring adopted the constitution on 14 October 1962. Both days are public holidays: Independence Day and Constitution Day. The British had kept the Italian place and street names, and the country kept a continental cast in its institutions, among them its value added tax. It built a protected economy around state mining, state energy and its own manufacturers, and opened it in the early 1990s. In 1994 it joined [[Bayvarra]] and [[Lisavu]] in the [[Lumeport Trade Accord]].

sections.title: Economy
sections.text:
Urvania's economy grew around the mine, the energy companies and the works of [[Ferrano]], among them [[Valdara Industries]], the bench maker founded in the year of independence. Its energy market is unbundled: a power station produces electricity, a grid operator runs the networks and a retail company supplies the customers. The country levies a value added tax at every stage, deducted by businesses and not charged on exports.

Urvania uses about 3 TWh of electricity a year, with a peak of about 550 MW. About two-thirds comes from water: the Nevola hydro scheme in the massif, a dam that holds the Lago della Nevola and a power station of about 300 MW, built from 1956 to 1961, and run-of-river plants on the upper [[Runmek]] and the [[Pastora]] of about 120 MW together, built in the 1960s. The sun gives about a tenth: the Saline Brune solar park of about 150 MW, on the dry salt-marsh edge behind the south coast, opened in 2018, and the roofs of homes and farms, which sell their surplus. When the sun shines the reservoirs hold back their water for the evening. [[Montebrio Power]] covers the peaks and the dry years, and the rest is bought from [[Bayvarra]] on the Accord's wholesale market.

sections.title: Languages
sections.text: Urvanian and English are official. Place and street names are the Italian ones, which count as English; Urvanian gives every place its own name too, and addresses carry both.

XB.name: Bayvarra
XB.note: Mainland, in the east, on the estuary. Distribution, retail, the seaport and the airport hub of Lumeport.

currency.name: Lume
currency.note: ISO 4217 style: the country code and the initial of the currency's name; checked against the current ISO 4217 list. Two decimals, the most common case.

wiki.lead: The **lume** is the currency of [[Bayvarra]], divided into a hundred parts.

sections.title: Exchange
sections.text: The lume is the anchor of the [[Lumeport Trade Accord]]'s fixed parity, in force since 1996: one lume is worth a hundred ferra or four tenths of a coral.

tax.summary: A federal country: its states, and the federal territory in the north, levy a retail sales tax, charged once, on the final use. A sale for resale or manufacture (goods sold on as they are, or that become part of the product sold, the packaging that goes to the customer included), exports, sales to public bodies and services to a business are exempt, and the invoice says so; what a business uses up or keeps (fuel and energy it burns, consumables, tools, machines, vehicles, buildings) is taxed as a retail sale, at the rate of the state where it is delivered.
tax.exemption_codes_note: The exemption reasons as codes of Bayvarra's national list (XB:TaxExemptionReason).

duty_free.note: Bayvarra's tariff charges no duty on medicines (HS chapter 30) nor on radioactive isotopes and their compounds (HS 2844.43, which holds the technetium generators of nuclear medicine), whatever their origin, as most countries apply under the WTO's zero-for-zero agreement on pharmaceutical products.

withholding.note: The public body withholds 10 % of the price and pays it to the state for the supplier; a non-resident supplier appoints a tax representative in Bayvarra.

wiki.short: Federal country on the plateau and the east coast of the mainland
wiki.lead: **Bayvarra** is a federal country on the mainland, east of [[Urvania]], with about {population} people. It holds most of the plateau, the dry east and the low north coast. Its capital and port city is [[Lumeport]], at the narrows of the estuary. Its currency is the {currency} ({currency_code}).

sections.title: Geography
sections.text:
Bayvarra covers about 70,100 km². The plateau of Upland State falls to the dry east of Coastal State, a land of grazing and wheat; the north coast is low. The [[River Lark|Lark]], the largest river of the east coast, reaches the sea at [[Larkmouth]]; the [[River Tallow|Tallow]] and the [[River Marrow|Marrow]] drain the plateau south to the [[Runmek]]. On the slope north of [[Marrowdale]] lies the Upland State Forest, planted and felled by compartment.

Bayvarra shares the mainland's climate: dry, sunny summers with light north-east winds, and winters of westerly winds and fronts. The winter rain falls on the western high ground, so Bayvarra's east and north-east, in its rain shadow, are the driest land of the mainland, with about 500 mm a year, and the sunniest.

The settlers named the plateau the Upland, which gave Upland State its name; the grazing land of the dry east, drained by the [[River Sallow|Sallow]], is the Sallow Downs; the low, thinly peopled north coast is the Gull Coast, after Gullhaven; and the headland behind which the first settlers landed at [[Larkmouth]] is Lark Head.

sections.title: Government
sections.text: Bayvarra is a federal parliamentary monarchy under the British Crown, represented by a governor-general. The federal parliament has a House of Representatives and a Senate in which the two states have equal seats; the Northern Territory sits in the House only. Each state has its own parliament and government. Bayvarra has two states and a federal territory. Upland State lies inland on the plateau, with [[Marrowdale]]; Coastal State lies along the east coast, with [[Lumeport]] and [[Larkmouth]]; the thinly peopled Northern Territory holds the low north coast, with the fishing village of Gullhaven. Each levies its own rate of the retail sales tax, charged once, on the sale to the final consumer: 5 % in Upland State, 6.5 % in Coastal State and 4 % in the Northern Territory.

sections.title: History
sections.text:
British settlers landed at [[Larkmouth]] on 16 February 1824, at the mouth of the largest east-coast river, and spread over the dry east and the plateau as graziers and wheat farmers; Bayvarra keeps the landing as Settlers' Day, on the third Monday of February. In the late 1830s their company kept a trading station at the narrows of the estuary. After the Urvanian rulers' treaty with Sardinia in 1840, Britain annexed the coast and the dry east on 29 November 1841, fortified the station and laid out [[Lumeport]] there as the colony's seat; Coastal State keeps the day as Coastal State Day, on the last Monday of November. As the river trade grew, Lumeport took over from Larkmouth as capital in 1852. Few people lived on the dry east and the plateau; the Urvanian peoples lived in the valley, which stayed theirs under Sardinian protection. A boundary convention of 1857 set the border with [[Urvania]] along the Runmek and the watershed, and on 12 April 1858 the plateau became a colony of its own, Upland; Upland State keeps the day as Upland State Day, on the second Monday of April.

In the late 19th century the two colonies built their railways, and villages grew at the stations. On 16 October 1899 they joined as the federation of Bayvarra, a self-governing dominion under the British Crown, with the low north coast as federal territory; Bayvarra keeps the day as Federation Day, on the third Monday of October. It took over its own foreign affairs and its last ties to the British Parliament step by step and was fully sovereign by the early 1930s. In 1974 it signed the Lumeport Agreement with [[Lisavu]], and in 1994 the [[Lumeport Trade Accord]] with both its neighbours.

sections.title: Economy
sections.text: Bayvarra's economy is a trading one: distribution, retail, the seaport and the airport of [[Lumeport]], and the wool, wheat and timber of the plateau. Since 2011 gas from an offshore field off the north coast is sold by pipeline to [[Urvania]]. In the dry north-east, the sunniest part of the mainland, solar farms on the Sallow Downs sell their power into the Accord's wholesale market, much of it across the border to Urvania. They stand on grazing land, where the sheep still graze between the panels, and belong to a company the graziers own together with the [[Bank of Lumeport]], which financed them.

XL.name: Lisavu
XL.note: Island, about 1,100 km east of Lumeport, reached by sea and air. Cotton, and a buyer of the mainland's goods.

currency.name: Coral
currency.note: ISO 4217 style: the country code and the initial of the currency's name; checked against the current ISO 4217 list. Three decimals, as with the Bahraini or Kuwaiti dinar.

wiki.lead: The **coral** is the currency of [[Lisavu]], divided into a thousand parts.

sections.title: Exchange
sections.text: The coral was tied to the lume by the Lumeport Agreement of 1974, at two and a half lume to the coral. The [[Lumeport Trade Accord]] kept that rate when it brought the ferra into the parity in 1996.

tax.summary: An island without a general sales tax or VAT: the state is financed by customs duty and an import consumption tax, both collected by customs at import. Domestic sales carry no tax, and the invoice says so.
tax.exemption_codes_note: The exemption reasons of the import consumption tax as codes of Lisavu's national list (XL:TaxExemptionReason): medicines and vaccines supplied to a public hospital.

duty_free.note: Lisavu's tariff charges no duty on medicines (HS chapter 30) nor on radioactive isotopes and their compounds (HS 2844.43, which holds the technetium generators of nuclear medicine), whatever their origin: an island that cannot make them keeps them cheap, as most countries do for medicines, many under the WTO's zero-for-zero agreement on pharmaceutical products.

withholding.on: the price of farm produce bought from farmers, by the buyer
withholding.note: A presumptive income tax: the buyer withholds 1 % of a delivery's value up to 2,000 coral and 2 % above, and pays it to the Island Customs Service, the island's only tax office.

tax_id.format: the companies register number; there is no separate tax number

address.line_rule: A line is made of the fields named in it, in that order, separated by a space; a field the address does not have is left out, and a line without any field is left out. A field with two language versions (street and town names in a bilingual country) gives both on the line, the national language first, then ' / ', then English: the building number is written once. Fields that are not on a line (ID, AddressTypeCode, CountrySubentityCode, TimezoneOffset, LocationCoordinate) say something other than where the post goes. The country is the last line of a postal address and is not repeated in the lines.

public_registry.name: Government list of public bodies of Lisavu
public_registry.note: The island's government keeps a short list of its public bodies (the customs service, the chamber of commerce, the maritime administration, the Department of Agriculture) and gives each a number of its own, derived from no other register.

system.name: Coral net of the Bank of Selanu

ledger.note: Coral net settles tokenised coral deposits on the Bank of Selanu's permissioned ledger; an account on it names the ledger.

payment.note: Island practice: longer terms, simple interest on late payment.

statutory_interest.note: Lisavu's statutory interest on late payment, which applies wherever neither a contract nor the seller's terms say anything on late payment.

cotton.note: The cotton fund of the Selanu Chamber of Commerce is financed by a levy of 1 % of the value of seed cotton sold, which the farm collects from the gin on the fund's behalf. Seed cotton is priced from the Trade Accord's lint reference price, published in lume by the Lumeport Trade Accord Council.

phone_plan.note: A small island: 7-digit numbers without area codes; fixed lines start with 72, mobiles with 77, ships with 79.

XL.legal_forms_note: The legal forms of Lisavu as codes of its national list (XL:CompanyLegalForm), with the abbreviation a company's registered name ends in.

customs-trader.name: customs trader number of Lisavu

wiki.short: Island country in the South Atlantic, east of the mainland
wiki.lead: **Lisavu** is a volcanic island about 1,080 km east of [[Lumeport]], with about {population} people. Its capital and only town is [[Selanu]], on a sheltered bay of the east coast. Lisavan and English are spoken. Its currency is the {currency} ({currency_code}), counted in thousandths.

sections.title: Geography
sections.text:
The island is about 116 by 85 km and 7,100 km², an eroded volcano that rises to about 1,810 m at [[Mount Tapetu]], some 25 km inland from the west coast, with the caldera called the Cauldron at its top, and falls to the east; a younger cone, [[Signal Hill]], about 780 m, stands above Selanu. The west coast, the Weather Coast, faces the westerly wind and the ocean swell: cliffs, bays where the land has slid into the sea, the largest of them Ketahe Bay, stacks and islets, and no port. Ships round Cape Sihato in the north or Cape Lavase in the south to the lee side, where the port and [[Selanu]] lie. The airport stands on the plain about 10 km north of the town, and the cotton grows on the Cotton Plain, about 690 km² in the dry north-east, in the island's rain shadow.

Lisavu lies about 33° south, on the edge of the westerlies: its wind blows from the west nearly all year, from the south-west in summer and strongest in winter. The windward west catches the rain, up to about 4,800 mm a year on the high ground, while the plain in the north-east, in the lee, has 640 to 760 mm and long sunny spells. The coast has about 20 °C in the warmest months and 15 °C in the coolest; the summit, about 12 °C colder, has snow in some winters.

sections.title: Government
sections.text: Lisavu is a constitutional monarchy of the line of its Lisavan rulers. The ruler is head of state; an elected Island Assembly makes the laws, and a chief minister leads the government's departments, whose central office is the Government Secretariat.

sections.title: History
sections.text:
The Lisavans' tradition tells of ancestors who came over the sea by canoe, steering for the peak of [[Mount Tapetu]], turned east round Cape Sihato and landed in the most sheltered bay of the north coast, at Natahoma, where the oldest village sites on the island lie, about 2,000 years old. In the centuries after, villages spread along the sheltered lee coasts and onto the landslide flats under the west cliffs, living on their gardens and on fishing. By about the 14th century the island stood under one line of rulers, seated at the village on the east bay that gave [[Selanu]] its name. Each spring the elders of every village met at the rulers' meeting ground there, the [[the Litakima|Litakima]], a custom the island keeps as Elders' Day. The first European ships, Portuguese and Dutch, called in the 1600s for water; from the 1790s whaling ships called regularly, and the rulers traded fresh food with them. In the 1860s, when cotton was scarce in the world, English settlers laid out cotton estates on the dry north-eastern plain, at Lintwell and Bollworth, on land leased from the Lisavan rulers, and built their town, Port Wrenfield, on the wharf beside the village. In 1878 the rulers, the estates and the merchants of Selanu founded the [[Bank of Selanu]] to finance the crop and the island's trade overseas.

From 1884 the island was a protected state of Britain: Britain handled its foreign affairs, to secure the cotton trade and keep other powers away, while the Lisavan rulers kept governing at home. On 7 July 1962, the year Britain also left [[Urvania]], the island took back its foreign affairs and became fully self-governing; it keeps the day as Island Day. In 1974 it signed the Lumeport Agreement with [[Bayvarra]]: its cotton entered Bayvarra free of duty, a regular shipping service linked the two, and the coral was tied to the lume. In 1994 it joined the [[Lumeport Trade Accord]].

sections.title: Economy
sections.text:
Cotton is the island's export. Lisavu has no general sales tax: customs collects an import consumption tax on every import, whatever its origin, and a duty on goods from outside the Accord.

The island's electricity comes almost wholly from water, sun and wind, run by the government's electricity department; as an isolated system it is exempt from the Accord's rule that networks be run apart from supply. The island uses about 110 GWh a year, with a peak of about 22 MW. The [[Tapetu (river)|Tapetu]] hydro plant of about 8 MW, built in 1968 as the island's first great work after self-government, takes the river high in its valley and brings it down a pipeline to a power house above [[Nihekemo]], and a small reservoir lets it run in the evening and at night. Two small plants of about 4 MW on the streams of the wet west slopes followed in the 1980s; a solar park of about 25 MW beside the airfield at Lintwell opened in 2015, with the roofs of Selanu; three wind turbines of about 12 MW on the high ground above the west cliffs came in 2019, and a battery store of about 40 MWh at Selanu in 2021. Since 2022 the old oil-fired station at Selanu is a reserve for dry, calm weeks only. The island is also cutting its use of fuel on the road: Selanu's buses and the town's delivery vans are being replaced by electric ones, while ships, aircraft, tractors and heavy trucks still run on fuel.

exchange_rates_note: Units of the second currency for one unit of the first, the reference rates of the world's frozen moment: 1 lume = 100 ferra, 1 lume = 0.4 coral. Against currencies outside the Accord the lume floats: the Lumeport Exchange's daily fixing.

A map square is 3.5 km each way, and coordinates keep that scale on both axes: a degree of latitude is 111.0 km, a degree of longitude 111.32 km times the cosine of the latitude of the area's centre. The drawn mainland (columns 11 to 170, rows 38 to 151, with a few islets just beyond) is centred on 30.0 degrees South, 15.0 degrees West, the middle of D19's box, and so lies at about 28.2 to 31.8 degrees South and 17.9 to 12.0 degrees West (D19's box of 28.1 to 31.9 South and 17.7 to 12.3 West is not quite 560 by 390 km; the kilometres win). Lisavu is drawn nearer, as an inset: its squares (columns 209 to 240, rows 100 to 123) are placed around its true centre, 33.0 degrees South, 2.65 degrees West.
geography.telephone_note: Telephone numbers use +999, a country code that the ITU reserves for a future global service (ITU-T E.164), so no number in the examples can reach anyone; the next digit is the world's country, and each country has its own numbering plan and number length (phone_plan).

payment_cross_border.name: Payment link of the Lumeport Trade Accord
payment_cross_border.note: Payments between the three countries run over the Trade Accord's link; charges are shared (ISO 20022 SHAR). The link settles in real time on a net basis (RTNS), and a payment the payer marks as not urgent goes in its batch run, a mass payment net system (MPNS).

qau.name: Urvanian
qau.note: The language of Urvania's original population, invented for the world, with a consonant-rich sound of its own (endings in -ek, -an, -ir). Urvania was an Italian territory and then under British rule; the British kept the Italian place and street names, while the people kept their Urvanian names for the same places. Since independence Urvania is bilingual, Urvanian and English, and the inherited Italian names count as English: they are never tagged as Italian. Code from the range ISO 639 reserves for local use (qaa–qtz); texts from a fixed invented vocabulary, word by word; the English text beside it is the reference.

wiki.lead: **Urvanian** is the language of [[Urvania]]'s original people and, beside English, one of the country's two official languages. It has a consonant-rich sound, with words ending in -ek, -an or -ir.

sections.title: History
sections.text: Under Italian and then British rule the place and street names stayed Italian, while the people kept their own Urvanian names. On 17 June 1951 the British administration made Urvanian an official language beside English, in the courts, the schools and the administration, after years in which the Urvanians had asked for it; independence in 1962 kept the bilingual state. Urvania keeps 17 June as Language Day.

sections.title: Place names
sections.text: Urvania's places have Urvanian names beside the Italian ones that the British kept and that now count as English: [[Ferrano]] is *Ruldraz*, Portaggio *Trenzir*, Fierabruna *Hihek* and Forte Euridice *Girkul*. Streets and towns are named in both languages, and an address gives both.

qal.name: Lisavan
qal.note: The island's language, invented for the world, with a Polynesian sound like the island's names: syllables of a consonant and a vowel, no clusters, words ending in a vowel. It is official beside English. Code from the ISO 639 local-use range; texts from a fixed invented vocabulary, word by word; the English text beside it is the reference. Its words are checked so that none is a common word of a real Polynesian language.
qal.english_place_names_note: The island's towns are known by their Lisavan names, which stay the primary ones; each also has the English name its English-speaking settlers gave it, official beside it, as Urvania's towns have their Urvanian and their English (inherited Italian) names. An address gives both, Lisavan first. The English names were checked so that none is a well-known real place.

wiki.lead: **Lisavan** is the language of [[Lisavu]] and, beside English, one of the island's two official languages. Its words are syllables of a consonant and a vowel, without clusters, and end in a vowel.

sections.title: Place names
sections.text: Most of the island's villages have Lisavan names only, among them Felulaka, Natahoma and Setahu. The villages of the 19th-century cotton estates have English names with Lisavan ones beside them: Lintwell (*Kefalasa*) and Bollworth (*Pakesa*). The capital keeps its Lisavan name, [[Selanu]], beside the English *Port Wrenfield*.

en.name: English
en.note: Bayvarra's language, official on the island beside Lisavan, and the working language between the three countries.

wiki.short: Working language of the Lumeport Trade Accord
wiki.lead: **English** is the working language of the [[Lumeport Trade Accord]], the language of [[Bayvarra]] and an official language of [[Urvania]] and [[Lisavu]], beside [[Urvanian]] and [[Lisavan]].

sections.title: Varieties
sections.text:
The three countries write English in the British manner: colour, harbour, centre, tonne; dates as 15 April or Monday 11 May; the 24-hour clock; a comma for thousands and a point for decimals. Each has its own variety.

**Bayvarran English**, the settlers' English, keeps plain words of its own, a truck rather than a lorry and a store for a shop, and ends an address with the town, the state and the postcode.

**Urvanian English** uses the Italian words of its streets and places as English, via, piazza, corso, strada, banchina, and gives amounts in whole ferra.

**Lisavan English** stands beside Lisavan on the island, calls the capital Selanu rather than Port Wrenfield, takes a few Lisavan words into its English, and gives amounts in coral to three decimals.

identifier_schemes_note: Identifiers from a scheme name it in schemeID (decisions ID-Q1 to ID-Q4). The Trade Accord's schemes and the real external ones are in identifier_schemes, by schemeID; each country's own are in its identifiers, by kind, with the schemeID urn:ubl-examples:world:<CC>:<kind>; a kind marked scheme false (call signs, MMSIs, driving licences, national ID numbers) has a format the world checks but no schemeID. The ITU call sign series and aircraft nationality marks QU, QB and QL, the MMSI maritime identification digits 297, 298 and 299 and the UIC country codes 46, 47 and 48 are not allocated to any real country (Fictional values). tools/world_ids.py checks them.
card_schemes_note: Card numbers follow ISO/IEC 7812: the major industry identifier 9 (national assignment) and the ISO 3166 numeric code of the issuer's country (901 Urvania, 902 Bayvarra, 903 Lisavu), then the issuer's two digits, the account and a Luhn check digit. A chip application identifier (ISO/IEC 7816-5) starts with the registered application provider identifier (RID) of the card scheme, from the national registration category D followed by the country code. A receipt shows the card number masked as the merchant's till does, at most the first six and the last four digits (PCI DSS), and never the security code or the card's dates.
documents_between_countries: Documents between the countries of the Trade Accord (sender and receiver in different countries, wherever the goods go) are in English, in the sender's variety (en-XU, en-XB, en-XL): a party states English with its own country's locale, and notes and code names come in English only. At home an Urvanian or Lisavan party states its own language (qau, qal), and its documents give their notes in both languages. A party's master data (address, legal form) is written as its register writes it, in both official languages of a bilingual country, in every document (2026-11-17).

TA-UTIL.note: The Trade Accord's term for utility bills (water, energy, telephone), the same in all three countries: due 21 days after the bill; a household with a direct-debit mandate is collected on that day.

payment_terms_note: Which payment terms an invoice applies, in three layers: what the parties agreed in a contract or framework agreement; where they agreed nothing, the seller's standard terms (XU-STD, XB-STD, XL-STD); where neither says anything about late payment, the statutory interest of the seller's country, where it has one. A cross-border sale follows the seller's country unless the contract chooses otherwise. Utility bills follow the Trade Accord's own term TA-UTIL.

road_rules_accord.note: The Trade Accord's road protocol: a tractor unit with its semi-trailer, or a truck with its trailer, may weigh at most 40 tonnes with its load on the roads of all three countries. A carrier's fleet gives each vehicle's empty weight, so its payload is what is left to the limit; the build checks that a weighed road load stays within both.

shop.name: Monday to Saturday
shop.note: Shops and warehouses that serve them.

always.name: every day
always.note: Ports, carriers, terminals, border customs and the operations of utilities; they work through the public holidays.

abroad_countries.note: Real countries outside the world that the world trades with (partly answering O51): only what the documents need. They are not countries of the world: no map, no registers, no tax of the world.

tax.name: Value added tax
tax.export: Goods exported outside the European Union are zero-rated under Dutch VAT: no tax is charged (category G).

tax.name: Goods and services tax
tax.export: An export of goods is a zero-rated supply under India's integrated goods and services tax (IGST Act 2017, section 16): no tax is charged (category G).

wiki.short: Free trade area of Urvania, Bayvarra and Lisavu
wiki.lead: The **Lumeport Trade Accord** is the free trade area of [[Urvania]], [[Bayvarra]] and [[Lisavu]]. It was signed in [[Lumeport]] in 1994 and entered into force on 1 January 1996, turning the Lumeport Agreement of 1974 between Bayvarra and Lisavu into a free trade area of all three countries. Its council, the [[Lumeport Trade Accord Council]], sits in Lumeport.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: In 1974 [[Bayvarra]] and [[Lisavu]] signed the Lumeport Agreement: the island's cotton entered Bayvarra free of duty, a regular shipping service linked the two, and the island's coral was tied to the lume. [[Urvania]] opened its protected economy in the early 1990s and joined its two neighbours in the Accord.

sections.title: Provisions
sections.text: Goods of Accord origin cross between the members free of duty. The three currencies, the ferra, the lume and the coral, stand at a fixed parity. Each member keeps its own taxes: the island stopped charging duty on its partners' goods and kept its import consumption tax, which falls on every import whatever its origin. Carriage between the members follows the Accord's uniform rules, and the members share code lists for their electronic business documents.

sections.title: Protocols
sections.text: Later protocols extended the Accord. The procurement protocol of 1999 opened the members' public tenders to suppliers from the partners under common rules. The payment protocol of 2003 set up the payment link between the three banking systems and the card schemes used across the Accord. The energy protocol of 2007 opened the wholesale trade in gas and electricity between producers, networks and suppliers, and asks that a network be run with its own accounts and management and be open to others on equal terms. The protocol of 2014 on electronic business documents gave the members a common agreement for exchanging them and the code lists they share.

sections.title: Public services
sections.text: The Accord's chapter on public services, part of the Accord since 1994, keeps the supply of electricity, gas, heat from a network, water and telephone to end customers a national matter: each member keeps its own utilities, public or under national licence, and no utility of one member supplies end customers in another; the energy protocol of 2007 brought gas under the chapter. The chapter sets a common minimum for the customers: a bill is due 21 days after it is issued; every bill carries a statement of consumption, with each connection, the meter readings and the period, and other parties' charges on lines of their own; meters are read at least once a year and payments on account are settled each year; a household is cut off for non-payment only after written notice of at least 14 days; and each member names a body that hears customers' complaints. Every utility of the three members is public today: owned by the state, by a state of the federation, or run as a government department.
